name: Inpainting and Object Removal

# Inpainting and Object Removal


## Overview
This family removes unwanted objects or fills occluded regions in a pre-trained [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) representation [Parent]. Unlike [standard NeRF training](#985-nerf-training-loop-with-random-ray-batching.md) which reconstructs the entire scene from input views, these methods optimize the NeRF parameters to erase specific masked regions while maintaining geometric and photometric consistency across all unmasked views [Parent]. They are distinguished from sibling methods by their reliance on external 2D priors (such as inpainted images or [diffusion models](#10443-diffusion-models-ddpms.md)) to guide the 3D optimization, rather than relying solely on multi-view geometry or semantic segmentation alone [Parent].

## Shared principles
All methods operate on a pre-trained NeRF representation $f_\theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \to (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$ as defined in [Parent](12494-nerf-editing-and-inpainting-procedures.md). The core mechanism involves an optimization loop that minimizes a loss function $L$ to update the NeRF parameters $\theta$ [Parent].

The general optimization objective is:
$$
L = L_{render} + \lambda_{guidance} L_{guidance} + \lambda_{reg} L_{reg}
$$
where $L_{render}$ is the standard [photometric reconstruction loss](#7799-photometric-reconstruction-loss.md) on visible pixels, $L_{guidance}$ incorporates external priors (e.g., 2D inpainted images, diffusion model gradients, or semantic features), and $L_{reg}$ prevents artifacts or overfitting [G].

Key shared components include:
1. **Masking/Selection:** A binary or probabilistic mask $M$ or selection field identifies the region of interest (ROI) or occluded areas [Parent].
2. **External Priors:** Methods rely on 2D priors to guide 3D changes, commonly using diffusion guidance (e.g., [Score Distillation Sampling](#21179-score-distillation-sampling-sds.md) from text-to-image models) or semantic/text features (e.g., CLIP or LSeg) to align rendered features with prompts [Parent].
3. **View Consistency Enforcement:** To prevent inconsistencies across views, methods enforce [multi-view constraints](#14458-multi-view-constraint.md) through implicit geometrical and photometric priors embodied by the neural network, which automatically propagates single-view edits to all views [Parent].

The optimization loop proceeds as follows:
> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def optimize_nerf_inpainting(nerf_model, rays, masks, guidance_priors, lambda_guidance, lambda_reg, num_steps, lr):
    """
    General optimization loop for NeRF inpainting.
    Args:
        nerf_model: Pre-trained NeRF MLP.
        rays: Batch of camera rays with ground truth colors.
        masks: Binary masks (1 for masked/occluded, 0 for visible).
        guidance_priors: 2D prior colors for masked regions.
        lambda_guidance, lambda_reg: Loss weights.
        num_steps: Optimization iterations.
        lr: Learning rate.
    Returns:
        Updated NeRF model.
    """
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(nerf_model.parameters(), lr=lr)
    for step in range(num_steps):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        # Render current NeRF predictions for the batch
        rendered_colors = nerf_model.render(rays)
        # Photometric loss on visible pixels (mask = 0)
        loss_render = torch.mean((rendered_colors - rays.gt_colors)**2 * (1 - masks))
        # Guidance loss on masked pixels (mask = 1)
        loss_guidance = torch.mean((rendered_colors - guidance_priors)**2 * masks)
        # Regularization loss (e.g., weight decay or density smoothness) [G]
        loss_reg = torch.sum(torch.square(nerf_model.parameters()))
        # Total loss
        loss = loss_render + lambda_guidance * loss_guidance + lambda_reg * loss_reg
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    return nerf_model
```

## Subtopics

### [NeRF-In Inpainting Optimization](12372-nerf-in-inpainting-optimization.md)
A framework that removes objects using a single user-drawn mask and 2D color/depth guidance. It jointly minimizes color and depth losses to ensure consistency, avoiding the artifacts of using multiple inconsistent 2D priors.

### [Adaptive View Selection for Inpainting](12405-adaptive-view-selection-for-inpainting.md)
Addresses inconsistency by adaptively switching between 2D inpainting priors and multi-view geometry based on local texture gradients. It is chosen when maintaining multi-view consistency is critical to prevent flickering in textured regions.

### [Reference-guided Controllable Inpainting of NeRFs](13952-reference-guided-controllable-inpainting-of-nerfs.md)
Uses a single inpainted reference view to guide geometry and appearance via [back-projection](#2450-back-projection.md) and a bilateral solver. It ensures view-dependent effects (VDEs) and avoids the quality deterioration seen in methods requiring multiple inpainted views.

### Interactive Nerflets Editing
Selects individual objects using instance labels and manipulates the nerflet structure directly (e.g., copy-and-paste for duplication, deletion for removal) without additional optimization [S1]. It supports real-time volume-rendered RGB or depth images at up to 320 × 240 resolution while adjusting object bounding boxes [S1]. Performance benchmarks show 31 [FPS](#7182-farthest-point-sampling-fps.md) on 4 A100 GPUs with 64 [nerflets](#8263-nerflets.md), achieving 457 million sample evaluations per second at 192 samples/pixel [S1]. When deleting objects, empty scene regions will not carry any density after deletion, as there is nothing there to evaluate [S1].

## Background
The problem of 3D scene inpainting emerged as NeRFs became popular for novel view synthesis, where removing objects or filling holes required more than just 2D image editing [G]. Early approaches adapted 2D inpainting techniques to 3D by optimizing NeRF parameters [G]. The field has evolved to include diffusion-based guidance and reference-guided consistency [G].
